Class MeetJump

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.rl.MeetJump
public final class MeetJump extends Object
What it does about an opponent that is coming at it through the air: with its sword back and its feet on the ground, it runs in at that opponent while it is still going up, and swings the moment the game has it under the crosshair.

In the air it is W and the sprint key alone (the swing there has its own rule): thrown back by a hit, the way towards the opponent begins before it is down, and every tick of it counts.

Why. A critical hit can only be made on the way down. A player who jumps at the fighter for one is, for the six ticks of the way up, a player who cannot hurt it as he means to and cannot change where he is going. Left alone he comes down in reach and makes his hit. Met on the way up he is hit first, with a sprint behind it, and thrown back out of his jump: there is no critical hit, and the next hit is the fighter's. Standing still, or backing off, the fighter is only in reach of him when he is already coming down.

It overrides the swing being kept for the fighter's own way down (AnswerRule): that is for an opponent that is already there, and this one is not there yet.

Read from what the network is shown. No state.

    • dodges

      public static boolean dodges(float[] vec, boolean coming)
      Whether this is a tick to get out of the way of an opponent coming at it through the air: on its way up, coming, near, and the fighter's sword not back, so that it cannot be met (applies(float[])). S is held for it: a jump cannot change where it is going, and walking backwards for the six ticks of the way up keeps the fighter as far off as the jump carries the opponent in, so the critical hit comes down out of reach, or is not made. By the time the opponent can jump again the sword is back, and that jump is met.

      That is spacing as the players who space it do it: out of reach while the other sword is ready and its own is not, in again once it is. Before 19 October nothing did this, and on half the jumps made at it its sword was not back: the crit landed, and the sprint hit after it.

    • jumpIn

      public static int jumpIn(float[] vec)
      Whether the opponent is jumping in at the fighter now (on its way up, coming, near enough to land on it): 0 not, 1 with the fighter's sword not back in time to meet it, 2 with it back. For the reward that teaches it to keep its sword for that moment (RewardWeights.jumpInReady).

    • how

      public static int how(float[] vec)
      For the log: where this observation stops short of what applies(float[]) asks. 0: no opponent on its way up within range; 2: there is one, but its sword is not far enough back; 3: the two are not closing; 4: nowhere, which is applies(float[]).
